newsitem.title: THAILAND: FOCUS-Thai indicators paint shaky economic picture.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Thai indicators paint shaky economic picture.

text.p: Key economic data released on Thursday confirmed the Thai economy's fragile state with foreign reserves plunging and the balance of payments deficit soaring in May.
Foreign reserves dropped to a two-year low of $33.3 billion after the central bank aggressively defended the baht in May from attacks by foreign speculators.
The balance of payments gap expanded to 112.3 billion baht ($4.49 billion) from 15.5 billion baht in April, indicating heavy capital outflows.
A lack of confidence in the Thai economy was blamed for the pronounced weakness in the external balance, the central bank's chief economist Kleothong Hetrakul told a news conference.

Thailand is going through its worst economic slowdown in over a decade and is faced with high interest rates stifling business activity, a stock market now at eight-year lows and a baht that has been attacked by speculators.

The trade deficit in April almost doubled that of March to 41.0 billion baht while the current account deficit, which had shown signs of stabilising over the past four months, surged to 38.0 billion baht in April.

Kleothong played down the impact of currency controls imposed by the central bank in May to stave off speculative attacks on the baht. The controls cut supplies of baht to foreign players, creating a two-tier market, one onshore and the other offshore.
"The widened balance of payment deficit was caused by a drop in capital inflows to the non-bank sector," said Kleothong.
"Commercial banks also switched to foreign assets and the private sector scrambled to pay their foreign debt when the greenback eased...and during rumours of a possible baht devaluation," she added.
But Kloethong expressed optimism that the external balance picture would improve once the problems in the cash-strapped financial sector were solved.
Thailand's troubled finance sector is over-exposed to the depressed property sector and hit by a liquidity crunch.
The authorities have said they would announce new measures on top of some executive decrees made by the cabinet to facilitate mergers and consolidation among property firms.
Kleothong said the central bank would announce a plan of action in a day or two to rescue the troubled finance sector.

"We are in a transition period during which confidence must be restored. And that's what the authorities are doing. After the package is announced, we believe the sector will be more stabilised," she said but declined to elaborate.
"Capital movement is something that changes really fast. Once confidence is back, the money will return. With Thailand's underlying strong fundamentals, that could happen soon," she added.
On trade, Kloethong attributed the rise in April imports which rose to 151.4 billion baht from 149.1 billion in March to the purchase of a five-billion-baht satellite by Shinawatra Satellite.
Capital goods accounted for 77 billion baht or a 6.6 percent increase over the same period last year, indicating that manufacturing production could improve soon.
But April investment activities were subdued as financial institutions, hit by liquidity problems, non-performing loans and the economic downturn, were reluctant to expand credit.
The manufacturing production index rose 5.4 percent from the same period last year against 6.4 percent growth in March.
The private investment index also increased only 5.4 percent year-on-year compared with 5.8 percent in the previous month.
